title: Beyond the 956: Alan Osmond, eldest member of The Osmonds, dies at 76

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Alan Osmond, the eldest member of the chart-topping family act The Osmonds, has died at 76.

Osmond died Monday, November 2, 2026, at his home in Lehi, Utah, after decades with multiple sclerosis, according to The Associated Press. A family spokesperson said his wife, Suzanne Osmond, and their eight sons were with him at the time of his death. He had spent a week in intensive care before returning home Thursday on hospice care.

Born June 22, 1949, in Ogden, Utah, Osmond's musical career began in the 1950s, when he and his brothers Wayne, Merrill and Jay formed a barbershop quartet. The group grew into The Osmonds, a family act that became one of America's best-known musical families, moving from pop stardom to television and later to country music. Osmond was a talented songwriter and performer who helped write some of the Osmond Brothers' biggest hits.

In 1987, Osmond was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. The illness caused him to retire from performing with his family, but he remained a steady presence behind the scenes and in the family's public life. His son Doug Osmond told The Associated Press that his father never complained, living by the motto: "I may have MS, but MS does not have me."

Tributes poured in from his siblings. In a statement on social media Tuesday, Donny Osmond called his older brother his "protector" and "guide," saying he was "the one who quietly carried so much responsibility so the rest of us could shine." Merrill Osmond wrote that he had visited his brother two days before his death, and that even while struggling, Alan found the strength to chuckle at a joke and smile.

Osmond is survived by his wife, Suzanne; their eight sons, Michael, Nathan, Doug, David, Scott, Jon, Alex and Tyler; 30 grandchildren; five great-grandchildren; brothers Virl, Tom, Merrill, Jay, Donny and Jimmy; and sister Marie. His brother Wayne Osmond died in 2025 at age 73 after suffering a stroke.

Sources: The Associated Press; family spokesperson; tributes from Donny Osmond and Merrill Osmond.
